newsitem.title: USA: Terrace Holdings sees '97 revs of $14 mln.
newsitem.headline: Terrace Holdings sees '97 revs of $14 mln.

text.p: Terrace Holdings Inc said Thursday it expects 1997 revenues to be about $14 million, following the acquisition of Deering Ice Cream Co.
Terrace acquired Deering for 918,900 shares of its common stock plus warrants to purchase 250,000 more shares at $1.00 each. Shares in the company closed Wednesday at 2-1/8.
Terrace said none of its businesses will be divested at this time.

Terrace also said it will reduce the exercise price on its public warrants from $4.00 to $1.25 for a 60-day period, following U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission approval, expected in late May. After the 60-day period, the exercise price would return to $4.00.

Deering manufactures and markets frozen desserts under the names Deering and Howard Johnson. Terrace organizes Passover holiday vacations and owns a Kosher restaurant and several catering operations in South Florida.

Separately, Terrace said that it had filled two vacancies on its board of directors. Steven Shulman is a managing director of Latona Inc, an investment bank based in New Hampshire, and director of several private and publicly held companies. Richard Power is president of Carlisle Plastics Inc., a subsidiary of Tyco International.
